maya: Pushing up stratos9b int4 conversion to staging. quick sanity eval done, some odd long-context behavior.

sam: Nice — any numbers yet?

maya: small snapshot: SQuAD F1 78.1 -> 77.8 after quant, HumanEval pass@1 12.0 -> 11.8. embedding cosine (512 tok) mean 0.992 -> 0.988. Longctx (4k) embed cos drops more on some prompts though.

liam: I ran a headwise diff on rotary params after quantize step, looks like head 3 and 6 show a consistent phase shift vs fp16. failing assertion: `np.testing.assert_allclose(rot_orig[3], rot_q[3], atol=1e-2)`

maya: can you paste the diff or a tiny dump?

liam: sure — log snippet: ```head idx | max abs diff
0 | 0.003
1 | 0.002
2 | 0.005
3 | 0.028 <<
4 | 0.004
5 | 0.006
6 | 0.031 <<
```

maya: ugh. I converted with AWQ `--scale-per-head` off. tried rerun with `--preserve-rotary` flag (experimental) and longctx embed cos improved to 0.990, but saw a small drop on arithmetic tasks.

sam: could also be a tokenizer id offset. stratos vocabulary uses EOS=50255 in original; our converter assumes 50256. seen that cause kv-cache misalignment before.

ryan: yep, I remember a zephyr onboarding where sentinel/EOS index mismatch shifted token ids by 1 and produced subtle rotary phase misalignments. run `python convert_vocab.py --check-offsets`

maya: ran it. output: `found_offset: true, offset_map: {"50255":"50256", "40001":"40002"}` — a handful of indices remapped during conversion. I think our tokenizer build step applied NFKC and collapsed some tokens which changed indices.

liam: options: 1) quick shim at runtime to remap token ids before kv-cache (`kv_cache.remap(token_ids, offset_map)`), 2) rebuild vocab.json with canonical canonical indices and re-run conversion pipeline, 3) keep preserve-rotary but accept arithmetic drop.

maya: prefer (2) — fix conversion so downstream runtimes don't need hacks. I'll rebuild tokenizer without nfkc normalization and re-run conversion+quant.

sam: also observed latency differences between AWQ and GPTQ kernels: AWQ had higher tokens/sec in bulk but worse tail latency (p99) because of per-head re-scaling in our implementation. worth benchmarking properly: `bench_quant_kernels.py --model stratos9b --kernels awq,gptq --requests 1000 --concurrency 8`

maya: adding to TODO: AWQ vs GPTQ microbench + p50/p90/p99, and headwise per-head config (try `--per-head 0,0,1,1,0,...`) to see if quantizing some heads differently helps rotary-sensitive heads.

liam: I'll prepare head sensitivity report — will run gradient-free probe prompts and produce per-head MSE + embedding-cos table.

ci-bot: deploy/green stratos9b-int4-preserve-rotary passed CI: 7/7 checks.

maya: thanks. I'll do the vocab rebuild and re-conversion now, then re-run the staged evals (including a new dataset `stratos-longcoref-100` that Liam suggested). will report back in follow-up thread. :thumbsup:
